reader.requirement: At --std 85, after a successful DELETE on a relative file the record is gone on every access path: a random READ, REWRITE, DELETE or START KEY = of its number takes the invalid key (23), sequential READ NEXT and START NOT LESS skip it, and it stays gone after CLOSE and reopen.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior in RelativeConnector.Delete/Rewrite/Start/AttachStore and KeyedStore.Delete (StoreTable only shares stores; its sharing flag is SharingFacilityInEffect, off at 85 and on at 2023, which does not change one connector's own view)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf31_01 covers random READ, second DELETE, a later record and a sequential pass after reopen; not REWRITE, START = and START >= of the deleted number, or READ NEXT in the same open

reader.notes: DELETE removes the slot's key from the store's B-tree (KeyedStore.Delete), so every later Get or Seek sees no record. Access by a second connector to the same physical file was not probed: at 85 the file sharing facility is off, and opening one file through two connectors is the implementor's matter.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-131/d56.cob (runs/d56-001, --std 85), aimed at a file position indicator that names the deleted record (GR6 leaves it unchanged): START KEY = 7, DELETE 7 (00), READ NEXT -> 'SN 00 D_08' (READ GR4c selects the first EXISTING record >= the indicator); READ NEXT positioned on 8, DELETE 8 by key, READ NEXT -> 'SN2 00 D_09'; START KEY > 5 after 5 was deleted -> READ NEXT 'D_06'; sequential access READ Q_03, DELETE, READ -> Q_04. The deleted record is never made available on any path. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.3.4 GR4 (the text is in GR4); OK §1985:VIII.4.3.4 GR6 (the text is in GR6); OK §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR4 (the text is in GR4).
